description.value: A priest kept firing it after his church burned down around him, and kept firing it for three days after that, by every account that survived to tell the story. Nobody's found the priest. The gun turned up decades later, and it still shoots like something's aiming it besides you — called shots seem to land exactly where you meant them, as if the gun already remembers where the bullet goes.

cinderfall.incomplete: the flavor implies guaranteed accuracy specifically for Called Shot, matching the pre-confirmed absence directly ("No rule element guarantees an outright success... No Reroll rule-element key exists anywhere") and also depends on the unencoded called-shot parent. No stated number of any kind beyond the narrative claim. This card depends on (upgrades, extends, or is gated behind) another Ironsight card in this same package that itself ships rules: [] -- if the parent has nothing real to build on, the child has nothing real to extend either.
cinderfall.special: Called shots seem to land exactly where you meant them, as if the gun already remembers where the bullet goes. Not expressed as a rule element: the prose states no bonus, DC or frequency.
cinderfall.failureRange: no Failure Range (Old World -- ironsight.html:115, 'Old World (Legendary) never fails')
cinderfall.priceless: No price by design, not a gap -- an Old World Gun is 'always found, never bought outright' (ironsight.html:122), matching the corpus's other unique gun (weapon-ranged.the-last-word).
